problem_statement:
Enforce schema when using json_writer() or json_reader()
Hi,

I have reproduced the example in https://fastavro.readthedocs.io/en/latest/json_writer.html but I've changed some items of the `records` array in order to introduce some type mismatches.

```
from fastavro import json_writer, parse_schema
from io import StringIO

schema = {
    'doc': 'A weather reading.',
    'name': 'Weather',
    'namespace': 'test',
    'type': 'record',
    'fields': [
        {'name': 'station', 'type': 'string'},
        {'name': 'time', 'type': 'long'},
        {'name': 'temp', 'type': 'int'},
    ],
}
parsed_schema = parse_schema(schema)

records = [
    {u'station': u'011990-99999', u'temp': 0, u'time': 1433269388},
    {u'station': u'011990-99999', u'temp': 22, u'time': "last day"},
    {u'station': u'011990-99999', u'temp': -11, u'time': 1433273379},
    {u'station': u'012650-99999', u'temp': 111.9, u'time': 1433275478},
]

text_stream = StringIO()
json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records)
print(text_stream.getvalue())
```

The 2nd row now has a string `time` instead of a long.
The 4th row now has a float `temp` instead of a int.

So clearly, some of the records doesn't respect the avro schema.

When I run this code, I get this output:

```
{"station": "011990-99999", "time": 1433269388, "temp": 0}
{"station": "011990-99999", "time": "last day", "temp": 22}
{"station": "011990-99999", "time": 1433273379, "temp": -11}
{"station": "012650-99999", "time": 1433275478, "temp": 111.9}
```

No warning, no error, the items are written as-is.

Same thing happens to the `json_reader`.
This code runs flawlessly:

```
from fastavro import json_reader
from io import StringIO

schema = {
    'doc': 'A weather reading.',
    'name': 'Weather',
    'namespace': 'test',
    'type': 'record',
    'fields': [
        {'name': 'station', 'type': 'string'},
        {'name': 'time', 'type': 'long'},
        {'name': 'temp', 'type': 'int'},
    ]
}

records = """{"station": "011990-99999", "time": 1433269388, "temp": 0}
{"station": "011990-99999", "time": "last day", "temp": 22}
{"station": "011990-99999", "time": 1433273379, "temp": -11}
{"station": "012650-99999", "time": 1433275478, "temp": 111.9}
"""

avro_reader = json_reader(StringIO(records), schema)
for record in avro_reader:
    print(record)
```

I would have expected these two snippets to raise an Exception because of incompatible types. Since I use a schema, I expect the encoder/decoder to respect it.

Is it possible to fix that in the library? Or maybe add a parameter to enforce schema validation?

Thanks.

diff --git a/tests/test_json.py b/tests/test_json.py
index e482961..def1a5a 100644
--- a/tests/test_json.py
+++ b/tests/test_json.py
@@ -661,3 +661,128 @@ def test_map_of_union_of_array_and_map():
 
     new_records = roundtrip(schema, records)
     assert records == new_records
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+
+_WEATHER_SCHEMA = {
+    "doc": "A weather reading.",
+    "name": "Weather",
+    "namespace": "test",
+    "type": "record",
+    "fields": [
+        {"name": "station", "type": "string"},
+        {"name": "time", "type": "long"},
+        {"name": "temp", "type": "int"},
+    ],
+}
+
+
+def test_json_writer_validator_true_raises_on_type_mismatch():
+    """When validator=True is passed, json_writer must raise an error
+    if a record doesn't conform to the schema."""
+    from fastavro._validate_common import ValidationError
+
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 0, "time": "last day"},
+    ]
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records, validator=True)
+
+
+def test_json_writer_validator_true_passes_valid_records():
+    """When validator=True is passed and the records DO match the schema,
+    json_writer must succeed and write the expected JSON output."""
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 0, "time": 1433269388},
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": -11, "time": 1433273379},
+    ]
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+    json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records, validator=True)
+    output = text_stream.getvalue()
+
+    assert "011990-99999" in output
+    assert "1433269388" in output
+    assert "1433273379" in output
+
+
+def test_json_writer_no_validator_is_backward_compatible():
+    """Without the validator argument, json_writer must NOT validate the
+    records — preserving the pre-fix behavior. Even mismatched records
+    must be written as-is without raising."""
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 0, "time": 1433269388},
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 22, "time": "last day"},
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": -11, "time": 1433273379},
+        {"station": "012650-99999", "temp": 111.9, "time": 1433275478},
+    ]
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+
+    json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records)
+    output = text_stream.getvalue()
+    assert "last day" in output
+    assert "111.9" in output
+
+
+def test_json_writer_custom_validator_callable_is_invoked():
+    """When validator is a custom callable, json_writer must call it once
+    per record with (record, schema, named_schemas)."""
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "A", "temp": 1, "time": 100},
+        {"station": "B", "temp": 2, "time": 200},
+    ]
+
+    calls = []
+
+    def my_validator(record, schema, named_schemas):
+        calls.append(record)
+
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+    json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records, validator=my_validator)
+    assert calls == records
+
+
+def test_json_writer_custom_validator_can_raise():
+    """A custom validator's exception must propagate out of json_writer."""
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "A", "temp": 1, "time": 100},
+    ]
+
+    class MyValidatorError(Exception):
+        pass
+
+    def my_validator(record, schema, named_schemas):
+        raise MyValidatorError("nope")
+
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+    with pytest.raises(MyValidatorError):
+        json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records, validator=my_validator)
+
+
+def test_json_writer_issue_reproduction_with_validator():
+    """Exact reproduction from the issue, but using the validator=True
+    parameter that the fix added. The 2nd record has a string time
+    (bad) and must trigger a validation error before all records are
+    consumed."""
+    from fastavro._validate_common import ValidationError
+
+    parsed_schema = parse_schema(deepcopy(_WEATHER_SCHEMA))
+    records = [
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 0, "time": 1433269388},
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": 22, "time": "last day"},
+        {"station": "011990-99999", "temp": -11, "time": 1433273379},
+        {"station": "012650-99999", "temp": 111.9, "time": 1433275478},
+    ]
+    text_stream = StringIO()
+    with pytest.raises(ValidationError):
+        json_writer(text_stream, parsed_schema, records, validator=True)
